risks.risk: Not actually working (motor/electrical faults, timing issues, or mechanical jam).
risks.proof: A short video of the machine powered on and stitching a straight line on fabric (show needle moving and feed working).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not working / needs repair until a live test is shown.

risks.risk: Missing or worn consumables/parts (needle, presser foot, bobbin case, belt, or damaged feed mechanism).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of needle, presser foot, bobbin/bobbin case area, and the underside/belt or motor connection (plus what accessories are included).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as incomplete/unknown parts until confirmed.

risks.risk: Wrong machine type for the buyer’s intended work (e.g., heavy-duty vs light-duty; industrial model may require specific setup).
risks.proof: Photo of the machine’s label/model plate (or a clear side view showing type) and a test stitch showing fabric thickness it can handle.
risks.if_unproven: Price it at the lowest practical category for an industrial sewing machine with unknown capability.

risks.risk: Hidden damage from drops/overuse (bent needle bar, cracked housing, worn gears).
risks.proof: Close-up inspection photos of the needle bar area, feed dogs, and any cracks/loose components; plus a test stitch video.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as potentially worn/needs servicing.

proof_requests: Send a video of the machine running and stitching (straight seam) with sound/needle movement visible.
Send clear close-ups of the needle area, presser foot, bobbin/bobbin case, and feed mechanism.
Send a photo of the model/serial plate (or any label) so the exact FLY model can be identified.
Confirm what accessories are included (needle, bobbins, presser feet, power cable/belt, foot pedal if applicable).
